A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhaseCoder/Gemma 3n research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and appendix reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original encoder localization experiments, fine-tuned Gemma results on four spatial-audio tasks, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds computational-efficiency measurements, a spatial-text Gemma baseline, and moving-speaker localization results.

M1.justification: The encoder architecture, positional embeddings, classification losses, two-stage training, spatial-token integration, and Gemma LoRA procedure remain unchanged. Added explanations clarify existing choices; the new text-based cascade is a comparison baseline.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 adds LOCATA Task 3, featuring a moving human speaker and stationary microphone array, beyond the previously evaluated Tasks 1 and 2. Existing training datasets and the four synthetic/RSL2019 LLM tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Gemma (2-stage), which receives PhaseCoder localization outputs as text, on both evaluation datasets. The new efficiency comparison also evaluates BAT's Spatial-AST in chunked and global modes alongside GI-DOAEnet. These substantially extend the comparisons beyond v1's encoder and spatially unaware LLM baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a computational evaluation using 10-second inputs, 2/4/8-channel configurations, memory/FLOP/latency measurements, and 250-ms versus 10-second Spatial-AST processing. It also introduces zero-shot evaluation with spatial coordinates sampled every 160 ms. Existing training budgets, decoding settings, and accuracy/WER protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The moving-source robustness test and representative trajectory in Appendix E/Figure 4 are new. Existing microphone-count sensitivity results, UMAP projections, reasoning breakdowns, model-size findings, and transcription examples are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Mean/median WER reporting and the appendix's correct/total counts are retained without a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds efficiency results, two Gemma cascade rows, and LOCATA moving-source MAE of 9.85 degrees. The cascade achieves 57.61% synthetic reasoning accuracy versus the unchanged fine-tuned model's 76.76%. Existing benchmark-table scores remain unchanged. v1's separate synthetic-summary statistics are replaced by discussion of the retained microphone-count results.

T1.justification: The positional-embedding and loss definitions, coordinate transformations, and label-discretization equations in Appendices A–B are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction adds computational efficiency to the encoder's stated contributions. The central claims about geometry-agnostic encoding, Gemma integration, spatial reasoning, targeted transcription, and localization performance retain their scope.

C2.justification: v1 says dynamic applications require future velocity/trajectory modeling; v2 removes that limitation and explains that independent 250-ms inference already supports moving-source localization. It also adds rationales for classification and token ordering, and attributes inference speed to transformer parallelism.

D1.justification: Unlike v1, v2 announces publicly released models and supplies a repository address. Appendix K documents the spatial-text baseline prompt, while Section 4.1 specifies profiling tools and GPU hardware. Android microphone-coordinate access guidance is also added. These substantially expand access and reproducibility documentation; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 discusses SpatialSonic, ViSAGe, SALM, and SmartDJ, positioning universal spatial encoders as potential controls for generation and editing. Profiling-software references are also added. The existing localization and spatial-LLM positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the prose, expands several explanations, adds conflict-of-interest and impact statements, and reorganizes the appendices. The main section sequence and most of the explanatory narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column conference formatting. The task-definition table moves to Appendix D and is expanded, a computational table and trajectory figure are added, Table 3 gains baseline rows, and existing appendix figures and tables are substantially reflowed.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important weakness in v1's validation by adding an LLM baseline explicitly supplied with spatial information, with its prompt documented in Appendix K. The efficiency comparison and moving-source evaluation also test practical properties previously unsupported by measurements. Together these substantially strengthen the evidence for the approach while retaining the original results. Model-release documentation further improves reproducibility, although neither version provides repeated-run uncertainty estimates.
